title: Keep, or delete?
prompt: You've inherited Splitwise-lite's test suite. CI takes 25 minutes and the team wants it faster without losing confidence. Select **every test you would delete** (or not write in the first place). Leave the ones that earn their place unselected.
hints: For each test, ask: what plausible bug would make it fail? If the answer is "only a refactor" or "only a bug in React", it is a candidate.
Regression tests for real bugs and tests of money edge cases are rarely the ones to cut.
explanation: Delete four. The whole-page snapshot fails on every markup tweak and teaches people to press "update" without reading. The `useState` test checks React, not Splitwise-lite. The constant test restates a line of code and can only fail when someone changes the value on purpose. The spy on a private helper fails on refactors and passes on real bugs. Keep the other four: the negative-amount format is a money edge case; the settle-up end-to-end test covers the flow where UI, API and logic meet; the regression test documents a bug that really shipped; and the 404 test covers error handling that users hit on bad links. To speed up CI, combine these deletions with sharding and moving duplicated end-to-end checks down to component tests.

page-snapshot.text: `expect(container).toMatchSnapshot()` on the entire rendered group page (a 400-line snapshot).
page-snapshot.why: Delete. It fails on every harmless markup change and says nothing about which behaviour matters, so reviewers rubber-stamp updates.

negative-format.why: Keep. Negative amounts and padding are exactly where money formatting breaks, and the test runs in a millisecond.

usestate.text: A test that renders a component, calls its `useState` setter through a test hook and checks the state changed.
usestate.why: Delete. It tests React's own behaviour, which React's suite already covers; it can't fail because of your code.

settle-e2e.text: A Playwright test: add an expense, click Settle up, expect "Everyone is settled up".
settle-e2e.why: Keep. It is the core flow, and only an end-to-end test checks that the UI, the API and the settle-up logic work together.

constant.why: Delete. It restates the source. It only fails when someone changes the constant deliberately, and then it just needs updating too.

private-spy.text: A test that spies on the internal `_sortDebtors` helper and asserts it was called exactly once by `settleUp`.
private-spy.why: Delete. It locks in an implementation detail: inlining or renaming the helper breaks it, while a wrong settlement would pass.

regression.text: A regression test from last spring's bug report: `expect(parseAmount('12.5')).toBe(1250)`.
regression.why: Keep. This bug actually shipped once; the test makes sure it never returns silently.

network-404.text: A test that `loadGroup` rejects with "HTTP 404" when the API answers 404.
network-404.why: Keep. Error handling is where bugs hide, and broken or old links make 404s a real user path.
